title: Foundation Landscape — Pressure, Door, Reproduction, Continuity and Return
purpose: Compress the 52-Foundation population into navigable historical patterns without replacing the full Foundation records or assigning moral altitude to whole entities.
reader_sequence: What pressure, opportunity or predecessor field existed before the Foundation?
What kind of Door changed what could operate?
What reproduced the Foundation beyond the original event or founder?
What continuity mode followed: living operation, branching, refoundation, merger, carrier loss or surviving Seed?
What returned to the World as practice, law, infrastructure, knowledge, service, art or capability?

trajectory_archetypes.label: Crisis → law / institution
trajectory_archetypes.pattern: rupture or coordination failure → charter/treaty/constitution → offices/procedures → public institutional return
trajectory_archetypes.lesson: The rising part is not the paper alone; durability comes from offices, procedures, interpretation and recurring operation.

trajectory_archetypes.label: Loss → portable community
trajectory_archetypes.pattern: destruction, execution, persecution or loss of center → texts/practices/community → branching beyond the original carrier
trajectory_archetypes.lesson: A physical or personal center can fall while a portable Seed becomes more important.

trajectory_archetypes.label: Need → mutual aid / service
trajectory_archetypes.pattern: material, health or social need → first local practice → repeatable group/service method → local branches
trajectory_archetypes.lesson: These Foundations often reproduce through meetings, roles and practice before they reproduce through abstract doctrine.

trajectory_archetypes.label: Experiment → method
trajectory_archetypes.pattern: bounded experiment → observable practice → handbook/training → independent copies
trajectory_archetypes.lesson: The decisive test is whether another group can reproduce the method without recreating the founder's exact circumstances.

trajectory_archetypes.label: Fragmentation → standard
trajectory_archetypes.pattern: incompatibility or access problem → specification/license/protocol → independent implementations → infrastructure
trajectory_archetypes.lesson: The Seed of Life is interoperability: many independent actors can coordinate without becoming one organization.

trajectory_archetypes.label: Manifesto / performance → movement
trajectory_archetypes.pattern: declared creative rupture → public naming/performance → cells/publications → historical influence
trajectory_archetypes.lesson: A movement can lose its original organization while its vocabulary and methods continue as transferable Seed.

trajectory_archetypes.label: Migration → new communal state
trajectory_archetypes.pattern: old environment blocks or cannot contain the next form → physical relocation → new agreements/practices → branching
trajectory_archetypes.lesson: Some Doors are literal journeys: the geography changes at the same time as the social state.

trajectory_archetypes.label: Venture / constraint → durable platform
trajectory_archetypes.pattern: resource or commercialization constraint → new company/venture structure → technical/operational reproduction → global platform
trajectory_archetypes.lesson: Enterprise Foundations reproduce through capital, specialist skill, suppliers, operations and governance—not merely founding intent.

trajectory_archetypes.label: Inquiry → school / programme
trajectory_archetypes.pattern: open problem or teaching lineage → stable place/text/programme → succession → later reception or application
trajectory_archetypes.lesson: The historical carrier can disappear while arguments, methods and training lineages remain active.

direction_synthesis.root_down: Find predecessor conditions, provenance, loss, material need and local substrate.
direction_synthesis.through_door: Identify the concrete threshold that changes what can operate.
direction_synthesis.sprout_up: Articulate a reproducible rule, practice, method, canon, standard or institution.
direction_synthesis.branch_out: Track chapters, schools, forks, implementations, denominations, offices and descendant organizations.
direction_synthesis.return_down: Test what the Foundation gives back to the World as capability, service, law, infrastructure, knowledge, art or nourishment.
direction_synthesis.drain_down: Use only for episodes where recurrence measurably reduces agency, correction, provenance or viable exit.
direction_synthesis.second_door: Use when merger, refoundation, revision or supersession carries selected residue into a new operating platform.
direction_synthesis.principle: Upward means increasing articulation/integration/transmissibility; downward can mean healthy rooting, harmful drain or accountable return. Direction is not moral rank.

homepage_projection.rule: Home teaches recurring patterns and selected examples. The Foundation Timeline owns the full 52-record genealogy.

records.name: Potatoism / Potato of Life
records.root_summary: Earlier Potato, meme and identity material is compressed into a mythic Seed rather than treated as a finished doctrine.
records.door_summary: The project crosses from persona/meme material into an increasingly explicit Potato-of-Life system, then crosses again in the 2025 Axis/Father-side refoundation.
records.sprout_summary: A repeatable project grammar becomes visible through the Potato of Life, Great Book, House, evidence classes and public repository.
records.fall_summary: Earlier formulations are repeatedly revised and absorbed; the current project explicitly preserves revision rather than treating old states as erased.

records.name: Danish constitutional order
records.root_summary: Growing opposition to absolute monarchy and the European political upheavals of 1848 make the old governing form insufficient.
records.door_summary: The written constitution replaces absolute monarchy with a constitutional order; later parliamentary practice and the 1953 constitution recross the Door without erasing continuity.
records.sprout_summary: Representative constitutional rules become reproducible through elections, institutions, courts and amendment procedures.
records.fall_summary: 1866, 1915, 1920 and 1953 revisions alter the operating platform; the foundation persists through amendment rather than collapse.

records.name: Constitution of the United States
records.root_summary: The Articles of Confederation framework is treated by the Philadelphia Convention as unable to support the desired federal coordination.
records.door_summary: Delegates sign the Constitution; ratification then satisfies Article VII and converts proposal into a legal operating threshold.
records.sprout_summary: Federal institutions begin operating under the new constitutional rules.
records.fall_summary: The constitutional foundation remains in force and changes through amendment and interpretation rather than a completed institutional fall.

records.name: Charter of the United Nations
records.root_summary: World War II devastation and the failure of the interwar collective-security order form the principal historical pressure field.
records.door_summary: The Charter is signed in San Francisco and crosses into legal force after the required ratifications.
records.sprout_summary: The UN becomes a reproducible international platform through membership, principal organs, procedures and treaty obligations.
records.fall_summary: Amendment, institutional change and new organs occur inside the continuing Charter foundation.

records.name: European integration / European Union treaty foundation
records.root_summary: Post-war distrust and the material capacity for renewed Franco-German conflict are converted into a problem of shared coal-and-steel governance.
records.door_summary: Successive treaties repeatedly cross the Door: Paris creates sectoral interdependence, Rome broadens integration, Maastricht refounds the structure as the European Union.
records.sprout_summary: Treaty rules become institutions, competences, markets and recurring amendment/accession procedures.
records.fall_summary: The ECSC treaty expired in 2002, but much of the integration lineage had already been transferred into later treaty structures; one shell ended while the broader foundation continued.

records.name: European Convention on Human Rights
records.root_summary: The experience of totalitarianism, war and mass rights violations creates pressure for binding supranational rights guarantees.
records.door_summary: The Convention is opened for signature in Rome and later enters into force.
records.sprout_summary: Enumerated rights and supranational review become a repeatable legal regime through applications, judgments, protocols and domestic implementation.
records.fall_summary: The rights regime is repeatedly amended and expanded; no terminal fall is recorded.

records.name: North Atlantic Treaty / NATO
records.root_summary: Post-war insecurity, Soviet expansion and fear that European states could not deter aggression separately create the alliance pressure field.
records.door_summary: The Washington Treaty is signed and enters into force after ratification.
records.sprout_summary: Collective-defense and consultation commitments become reproducible through councils, commands, strategic concepts and accession procedures.
records.fall_summary: Strategic concepts and membership change while the treaty remains the load-bearing reference.

records.name: International Monetary Fund
records.root_summary: Competitive devaluations, depression-era instability and wartime disruption create the problem field for a permanent monetary-cooperation institution.
records.door_summary: The Articles are adopted at Bretton Woods, enter into force, and later become operational lending/surveillance machinery.
records.sprout_summary: Quotas, rights, obligations, surveillance and lending become a reproducible institutional grammar.
records.fall_summary: Facilities, SDR rules and governance evolve through formal amendment rather than a completed fall.

records.name: European Central Bank
records.root_summary: The European Monetary Institute completes its preparatory role and is replaced by the ECB as monetary union moves from preparation to operation.
records.door_summary: The ECB replaces the EMI and assumes the institutional infrastructure needed for the single monetary policy.
records.sprout_summary: The ECB/ESCB institutional framework becomes operational and later supports the euro and Eurosystem.
records.fall_summary: The foundation changes through treaty interpretation, enlargement and added supervisory layers.

records.name: Danmarks Nationalbank
records.root_summary: War finance, state bankruptcy, inflation and loss of trust in banknotes create a literal monetary-system collapse before the bank's establishment.
records.door_summary: A new independent note-issuing institution is established to restore monetary trust; the 1936 Act later refounds/codifies it.
records.sprout_summary: Monetary functions and institutional independence become durable practices reproduced through law, staff, payment infrastructure and oversight.
records.fall_summary: The 1936 legal refoundation changes the shell while retaining the core safe-monetary-system purpose.

records.name: Christianity
records.root_summary: The execution of Jesus and loss of the movement's central teacher becomes, within early Christian memory and proclamation, a pivotal death-side event around which communities reorganize.
records.door_summary: The movement crosses from a teacher-centered circle into communities that transmit claims, practices and texts; later Nicaea is a major doctrinal consolidation rather than the first birth.
records.sprout_summary: Communities, ritual practice, oral/written transmission and later canon/creed structures make the movement reproducible beyond the first generation.
records.fall_summary: Schisms, councils, reforms and denominational branching alter the institutional shells while Christian lineages continue.

records.name: Judaism / Israelite-to-rabbinic formation
records.root_summary: Exile and, later, the destruction of the Jerusalem Temple in 70 CE remove or transform central political/cultic structures and create repeated refoundation pressures.
records.door_summary: Scriptural/Torah authority becomes increasingly central in the Persian period; after 70 CE rabbinic interpretation and community practice gradually provide another reproducible platform.
records.sprout_summary: Text, law, ritual, interpretation, community and later rabbinic institutions carry identity across loss of previous political/Temple forms.
records.fall_summary: The atlas should not assign Judaism one founding or one fall; its history shows several transformations where prior centers are lost and portable practices/texts preserve continuity.

records.name: Islam / early umma
records.root_summary: Opposition in Mecca makes continued communal development there increasingly untenable; the Hijra physically leaves the old operating environment.
records.door_summary: The Hijra is a literal geographic Door: movement from Mecca to Medina opens a new communal operating state.
records.sprout_summary: The early umma becomes a functioning community with new agreements, obligations and institutions in Medina.
records.fall_summary: After Muhammad's death, succession and legal/theological development produce multiple enduring branches and institutions.

records.name: Buddhism / early Sangha
records.root_summary: The seed begins as a problem of suffering, impermanence and the insufficiency of inherited answers for the seeker who becomes the Buddha; this is a doctrinal/problem-state, not a claim of institutional collapse.
records.door_summary: Awakening/teaching and the formation of a disciplined community convert individual search into a transmissible path.
records.sprout_summary: Teaching, Sangha and Vinaya make practice reproducible through successive communities.
records.fall_summary: Schools and canons differentiate; the atlas treats these as branching and refoundation rather than one fall.

records.name: Sikh tradition / Khalsa
records.root_summary: For the Khalsa refoundation, the execution of Guru Tegh Bahadur and intensifying political-military pressure form part of the rupture field inherited by Guru Gobind Singh's community.
records.door_summary: At Vaisakhi 1699 the Khalsa is inaugurated at Anandpur Sahib as a disciplined initiated order.
records.sprout_summary: Shared initiation, discipline, identity and institutions make the Khalsa a reproducible community form.
records.fall_summary: Military and political disruptions do not terminate the lineage; identity and institutions travel and branch.

records.name: Bahá’í Faith
records.root_summary: The Bábí movement undergoes severe persecution; Bahá’u’lláh's imprisonment and exile precede the Riḍván declaration and transform the predecessor field.
records.door_summary: The Báb's 1844 declaration seeds the predecessor movement; Bahá’u’lláh's Riḍván declaration in Baghdad marks a refoundation into the Bahá’í Faith.
records.sprout_summary: Writings, covenant and later elected administrative institutions create a durable global reproduction system.
records.fall_summary: The Bábí substrate is not simply erased; it is carried into a new religious identity and administrative order.

records.name: Daoist traditions
records.root_summary: Early Daoist texts, practices and cosmologies do not begin from one historical collapse; they are a distributed substrate later reorganized into institutional religious communities.
records.door_summary: The Celestial Masters tradition provides an early organized religious-community form traditionally associated with Zhang Daoling in the 2nd century CE.
records.sprout_summary: Texts, ritual offices, lineage, registers and community organization allow later Daoist traditions to reproduce and branch.
records.fall_summary: Schools repeatedly reorganize, absorb local traditions and refound institutions; no single terminal fall is modeled.

records.name: Confucian / Ru traditions
records.root_summary: The late Zhou/Warring States context supplies a problem of fractured ritual and political order rather than one discrete institutional death.
records.door_summary: Teachings and disciple transmission in Lu become a lineage; Han sponsorship and canon formation later convert that lineage into a durable state/educational tradition.
records.sprout_summary: Classics, commentary, education, ritual and bureaucratic institutions reproduce the tradition across dynasties.
records.fall_summary: Political regimes alternately elevate, reinterpret or suppress Confucian institutions; textual/educational reproduction allows later return.

records.name: Stoicism
records.root_summary: Cynic, Socratic and Megarian influences are recombined into a new teaching programme; the current Foundation record does not establish one singular death-side event.
records.door_summary: Zeno's teaching at the Painted Stoa gives the emerging school a stable public location and recognizable lineage.
records.sprout_summary: Teacher succession, argument, texts and practices reproduce Stoic philosophy beyond Zeno.
records.fall_summary: Ancient institutional lineages eventually fade, while texts and later receptions preserve transferable Seed.

records.name: Epicurean Garden
records.root_summary: Epicurus teaches earlier in Mytilene and Lampsacus before consolidating a stable community in Athens; no single rupture is required by the record.
records.door_summary: Purchase/use of the Athenian Garden turns a teaching network into a durable community with a place, succession and shared life.
records.sprout_summary: Community life, teaching, texts and succession make Epicureanism reproducible beyond the founder.
records.fall_summary: The ancient school declines while writings and later revivals preserve parts of the Foundation.

records.name: Platonic Academy
records.root_summary: Existing Socratic, mathematical and philosophical associations form the substrate; no single legal founding or one death-side rupture is historically warranted.
records.door_summary: Plato's group gathers sustained activity and property near the Academy, producing a recognizable school without a modern incorporation event.
records.sprout_summary: Scholarch succession, shared inquiry and teaching reproduce a Platonic lineage.
records.fall_summary: The Academy changes doctrinal orientation and later disappears as an ancient institution while Platonisms continue elsewhere.

records.name: Aristotle's Lyceum / Peripatetic school
records.root_summary: After long participation in Plato's Academy and later travel, Aristotle returns to Athens with an independent programme rather than continuing as an Academy successor.
records.door_summary: Aristotle rents buildings in the Lyceum and establishes a school there.
records.sprout_summary: Research collection, teaching and scholarch succession reproduce the Peripatetic programme.
records.fall_summary: The ancient school continues under successors but its collections and institutional coherence change; Aristotelian thought later re-seeds in other traditions.

records.name: University of Copenhagen
records.root_summary: Earlier 1419 authorization did not produce a functioning university; later the Reformation interrupts the Catholic institutional form and requires a 1537 refoundation.
records.door_summary: Papal authorization becomes an operating university in 1479; after the Reformation the institution crosses a second Door into a changed Lutheran/state role.
records.sprout_summary: Faculties, statutes, teaching, research and later governance reforms allow the university to reproduce through multiple political/religious regimes.
records.fall_summary: The Reformation changes the platform without ending the long institutional lineage.

records.name: Royal Society
records.root_summary: London- and Oxford-based intellectual gatherings lacked one durable chartered carrier; the first recorded meeting turns distributed practice into an institution.
records.door_summary: The 28 November 1660 meeting establishes a continuing Fellowship; the 1662 charter gives legal institutional form.
records.sprout_summary: Meetings, experiments, correspondence, fellows, publications and governance reproduce a scientific institution across generations.
records.fall_summary: The Society persists while governing charters and programmes are updated.

records.name: Montessori education
records.root_summary: The first Casa emerges inside a materially degraded housing environment where young children lacked provision, supervision and educational resources.
records.door_summary: A room is deliberately prepared and opened for the children, turning an unmanaged social problem into an observational educational environment.
records.sprout_summary: Prepared environment, materials, observation and later teacher training convert one experiment into a reproducible pedagogical method.
records.fall_summary: The method branches across countries and institutions; no single terminal fall is modeled.

records.name: Bauhaus
records.root_summary: After World War I, existing Weimar art-school structures are merged/recast into a new pedagogical programme.
records.door_summary: Gropius's directorship, renaming and manifesto turn predecessor institutions into the Staatliches Bauhaus.
records.sprout_summary: Workshop pedagogy, teachers, students, objects and buildings reproduce the Bauhaus programme across Weimar, Dessau and Berlin.
records.fall_summary: Political pressure forces dissolution in 1933, but emigrating members carry pedagogical/design patterns into institutions abroad. The physical school dies while the Foundation reproduces elsewhere.

records.name: CERN
records.root_summary: World War II fragmentation and the migration of scientific capacity from Europe create a need for shared peaceful infrastructure.
records.door_summary: UNESCO-backed negotiations become a signed Convention in Paris and then a legal organization after ratification.
records.sprout_summary: Member-state contributions, Council governance, laboratories, collaborations and training make large-scale scientific capability reproducible.
records.fall_summary: Accelerators and programmes end or are superseded while the institutional Foundation trains successors and builds new infrastructure.

records.name: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C)
records.root_summary: Rapid Web growth creates a risk that incompatible implementations and competing extensions could fragment a shared Web.
records.door_summary: Tim Berners-Lee establishes W3C at MIT/LCS as a dedicated standards coordination body.
records.sprout_summary: Working groups, specifications, conformance and international hosts allow Web standards to reproduce across vendors and platforms.
records.fall_summary: The hosted consortium model later changes into a public-interest nonprofit while standards continuity remains.

records.name: Wikimedia Foundation
records.root_summary: A rapidly growing volunteer knowledge project needs a stable nonprofit carrier beyond the original founder/company infrastructure.
records.door_summary: The Wikimedia Foundation is created under Florida law and the project assets are transferred into a nonprofit institutional base.
records.sprout_summary: Nonprofit governance, donations, staff, software infrastructure and volunteer communities reproduce a free-knowledge ecosystem distinct from one founder.
records.fall_summary: The Foundation later relocates headquarters and revises bylaws while the movement remains distributed.

records.name: A.P. Moller - Maersk
records.root_summary: The family shipping lineage had already survived a shipwreck and closure of an earlier family business; later A.P. Møller faced board resistance to fleet expansion.
records.door_summary: Father and son establish the Steamship Company Svendborg in 1904; A.P. Møller then creates the 1912 company to gain greater operational independence.
records.sprout_summary: Ownership, vessels, operational discipline and later logistics networks reproduce the enterprise beyond its initial founders.
records.fall_summary: The lineage repeatedly changes corporate form and business mix rather than showing a single terminal fall.

records.name: ASML
records.root_summary: Philips's wafer-stepper group faces uncertainty, failed partnership attempts and insufficient resources to commercialize the technology.
records.door_summary: Philips and ASM form a joint venture and ASM Lithography begins operations with inherited R&D, new autonomy and resources.
records.sprout_summary: A dedicated firm, staff, supplier relations, product platforms and repeated technical learning turn endangered R&D into a reproducible enterprise.
records.fall_summary: The founding story itself is a rescue from project failure; later survival depends on repeated technological refoundation rather than one static product.

records.name: Novo Nordisk
records.root_summary: Before insulin, diabetes was commonly fatal; the Danish insulin effort responds directly to that clinical condition. Later Novo and Nordisk exist as rival branches before merging.
records.door_summary: Insulin knowledge is transferred from Canada into Danish production; a second branch forms in 1925; the two lineages cross a merger Door in 1989.
records.sprout_summary: Insulin production, research, patient care, manufacturing and later merger continuity create a durable healthcare enterprise.
records.fall_summary: Competition produces two institutional branches; the 1989 merger recombines them into a new operating Foundation.

records.name: Rule of Saint Benedict
records.root_summary: Earlier monastic rules and ascetic practices provide the substrate; the current evidence does not require one discrete catastrophe as the Seed of Death.
records.door_summary: A written rule binds daily time, authority, work, prayer, admission and communal correction into a portable institutional grammar.
records.sprout_summary: Novitiate, schedule, governance and text transmission allow communities to reproduce the pattern across monasteries and centuries.
records.fall_summary: Monastic reforms such as Cistercian movements reinterpret the same rule rather than simply ending it.

records.name: TCP/IP Internet protocol foundation
records.root_summary: NCP and network-specific communication cannot provide the desired interoperable 'network of networks'; the old protocol is explicitly scheduled for shutdown.
records.door_summary: TCP/IP moves from design and experimental implementations to a flag-day conversion where ARPANET hosts must cross or lose ordinary network access.
records.sprout_summary: Open specifications, interoperable implementations and operating-system adoption let TCP/IP reproduce across independent networks.
records.fall_summary: NCP is deliberately switched off: one of the clearest literal technical examples of an old operating Seed dying as a new Foundation crosses the Door.

records.name: Unicode
records.door_place: Palo Alto / California → international standards network
records.root_summary: Incompatible platform, national and bibliographic character encodings make text identity and interchange unstable across systems.
records.door_summary: Unicode 88 states a universal design; incorporation creates a durable standards body; convergence with ISO 10646 prevents competing universal standards from hard-forking.
records.sprout_summary: Stable character identity, versioned data, conformance and implementations make the standard reproducible across platforms and devices.
records.fall_summary: The potentially rival Unicode and ISO 10646 paths converge, preserving a shared code space instead of one lineage simply destroying the other.

records.name: Rochdale cooperative model
records.root_summary: Low wages, poor working conditions and unaffordable basic goods create the immediate pressure that the Pioneers try to escape.
records.door_summary: Twenty-eight artisans pool scarce resources and open a member-owned store governed by explicit rules.
records.sprout_summary: Member stake, democratic voice, trading rules, education and surplus principles become portable cooperative Seed.
records.fall_summary: The original local experiment becomes a model reproduced by other cooperative forms and later coordinated internationally.

records.name: Newtonian mechanics / Principia programme
records.root_summary: Orbital motion, terrestrial mechanics and competing force accounts remain only partially unified; Halley's questions expose a problem demanding a stronger formal derivation.
records.door_summary: De Motu develops into Principia: a private mathematical result crosses into a registered, printed and teachable public programme.
records.sprout_summary: Laws, mathematical derivation, prediction, textbooks and engineering applications reproduce a classical-mechanics programme.
records.fall_summary: Relativity and quantum mechanics later constrain the domain of Newtonian mechanics without erasing its validity in the regimes where it remains an effective approximation.

records.name: Futurism
records.root_summary: Futurism explicitly defines inherited aesthetic forms and cultural immobility as something to break with; the 'death-side' is therefore partly self-declared manifesto rhetoric.
records.door_summary: Publication of the manifesto on the front page of Le Figaro converts a circle's programme into a public named movement; specialized manifestos then branch it.
records.sprout_summary: Manifestos, performances, exhibitions and stylistic imitation reproduce Futurist identity across artistic domains.
records.fall_summary: The current Foundation records do not yet carry a precise terminal clock; institutional movement activity declines while aesthetic influence persists in later art/design cultures.
